messages:
maria: Quick SCIM question — contract workers are still in our 'contractors' Okta group after their access tickets close. Should we be removing them via SCIM (delete) or setting active=false and let our offboarding job sweep them? Any security concerns with soft-delete?

sam: Short answer: set active=false via SCIM PATCH and have our offboard job remove after 7 days. Deleting immediately can break audit trails + interferes with downstream logs. Also ensure SCIM 'externalId' is the HR id so we don't recreate.

jess: +1 for soft-disable. Also make sure we redact PII from deprovision logs. Example regex we use: ```s/"email":"([^"]+)"/"email":"[REDACTED]"/g``` Logs should show userId only, not email.

leo: Note: if you're relying on the SAML group claim for runtime role mapping, disabling in SCIM won't remove SAML assertions until the IdP syncs. Okta emits groups in the SAML attribute `groups` — double-check mapping precedence in the app.

scim-bot: [2026-03-10T15:08:12Z] SCIM sync job failed for App 'okta-aws' — 409 Conflict on PATCH /Users/00u1abcde. Skipping. See /ops/scim-retry.

maria: Thanks all — jess can you update the runbook to include the regex redaction + the 7-day sweep? @jess

jess: Yup I’ll add it today and include a sample `PATCH /Users/{id}` body we use:
```json
{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"replace","path":"active","value":false}]}
```

sam: Also add a note: if the user is re-hired within 30 days, HR reactivates instead of reprovisioning to preserve links.

maria: Perfect, thanks :thumbsup:
